chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶2:**

The Divine
 Human extended its own
 life out
ward into separated
 and
 scattered
 states,
 distrib
uting the
 faculties of the
 living
 spiritual
 life —
 as
 has
 been set
 forth.
 Yet
 the Divine
 did
 not make
 itself known openly
 in
 these
 states:
 rather
 the
 blessed
 and
 glorious Divine
 itself
 entered
 imper
ceptibly into the interiors,
 according
 to the form of Divine good and the
 form
 of Divine truth,
 through
 Divine
 love itself,
 and
 through the pure affection of wisdom
 —
 which is the recept
ive capacity
 of truth
 proce
eding from the Divine love
,
 the
 in
most life
 of the Father
.

**¶3:**

Consider
 this
 by
 way
 of the external
 person
: just
 as every
 faculty
 of the natural
 mind
 depends upon its
 governing
 in
most principle, so that if any out
ward capacity
 is lost while
 the inmost love
 and
 understanding remain, there is hope
 of
 restoration —
 but if the inmost governing principle
 is severed, the entire spiritual life
 perishes and
 the
 person is utt
erly lost.

**¶4
:**
So
 it
 is with
 the Divine
 Human
.
 It
 is itself
 the inmost governing principle,
 and the
 goods
 and truths that proceed from it are
 as
 the faculties of its
 own
 spiritual life,
 attached
 to it
 as
 members
 to
 a head
. Or
, said
 another
 way:
 as
 the universal
 spiritual
 atmosphere
 —
 the Divine proce
eding life
 — sust
ains all who
 live
 and
 receive
 infl
ux from it
, so the
 Divine
 Human is that
 life
.
 And this
 governing
 principle pres
ides over the whole order of return and
 asc
ent through
 which
 all things rise
 toward
 the Divine —
 the universal
 column
 of glor
ification that
 extends
 through
 every
 degree
 of the
 created
 world
.

**¶5:**

So
 it is also
 with the Divine
 itself
:
 it
 is as
 the in
most principle governing every
 derivative state
,
 and as
 the sust
aining life established
 over
 the whole
 order of spiritual
 ascent. It
 is made powerful
 through
 the pure affection of Divine truth —
 which is its
 own wisdom
, the receptive form
 that
 the Divine love inv
ests with external truths as
 with
 gar
ments.

**¶6:**

These
 are
 the fac
ulties that
 proceed from the Divine:
 the
 interior
 mind
, the
 capacity
 for thought, the
 faculty
 of spiritual
 insight, the power
 of deliber
ation,
 and refl
ective disc
ernment — these
 it
 brought
 forth and sent out
 from
 itself
 to accomplish
 the
 Divine purpose
. And
 the
 Divine itself followed
 after
 its
 own proce
eding wisdom,
 desc
ending into those
 states where the
 living
 spiritual
 life had
 become ent
angled and
 held
 captive among
 fals
ities and evil affections — for
 these capt
ive elements
 of
 spiritual
 life are as scattered
 faculties of one
 body
,
 dispers
ed throughout
 every
 degree of the created
 order.

**¶7:**

And
 when these
 fac
ulties of
 understanding
 were sent forth
, the
 Divine was
 found united
 with the pure
 affection of truth, and
 it
 rose
 up,
 interc
eding and
 calling
 forth
 power
 from
 the in
most.
 And
 there
 was given
 the
 peace that
 belongs
 to heav
enly order
,
 and conjunction
 through mutual love, and the perception
 of del
iverance. Then
 the Divine Human
 itself
 gave forth its own
 life
 into
 its
 scattered
 fac
ulties and
 gathered together
 its separated
 spiritual life, and
 it
 established
 that
 life
 in its proper
 order
 as a complete doc
trinal form
 —
 an
 entire
 structure
 of wisdom,
 built
 up whole
.


**¶8:**
It
 arranged
 and perf
ected that
 restored
 spiritual life with
 Divine
 skill
, giving
 it heav
enly form.
 And
 the Divine
 tru
ths it
 had
 sent forth as
 living
 communications penet
rated in
ward and extinguished the falsities
 that
 had opp
ressed and
 crushed the spiritual life under
 the power
 of evil. All
 that
 had
 been scattered was
 gathered in
.
 All
 that had been displaced
 returned
 and
 was
 made
 firm
 once more —
 restored
 to the likeness of the Divine from
 which
 it had proceeded
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Indeed, the First Man dispersed himself and he [gave forth every] limb of the living soul as I have written for you [concerning the limbs] of the living soul; he has [concealed himself, and] he did not know [himself to them;] but the blessed, glorious Man came [in] secret; in his image; in his shape; in his love; in his holy virgin, she who is the virgin of light, the soul of the father.

After the fashion of this fleshly body: as the root of all the limbs hang upon the head, so that should one of the person's limbs be cut off, while the head exists he has hope for [its restoration;] but if his head should be cut off, the entire body will die and he is lost.

This is also the case for the Firs[t] Ma[n]. He is the head, while his sons attach to it the limbs [of] his soul. Or, conversely, like the living air, on which all flesh entirely lives as it breathes and [draws life] therein. His head is placed on the body of the Pillar of Glory in the heights of the universe.

[This i]s also the case [for] the father, the blessed Man; as he is like the head that is upon the body and the air that upon the Pillar is set i[n the heights,] being made strong by his light virgin, [she] who is his soul that he clothes [with his garments of light.]

[And these are] t[h]ose [five powers of his]: the mind, thought, insight, counsel and c[on]sideration that he produced and sent forth from hi[m to] do his will. He sprang and travelled behind them. [He came for the deliverance] of his living soul, which is entwined among the rebels; as they are like the limbs of its body, and [are dispersed throughout the] universe.

And when they were sent, at [that ti]m[e] he was found with the Virgin of [Lig]ht and [he] stood up, asking and entreating for a p[o]wer. [And the Father] gave him peace and a ki[ss. And] he [gave] him goo[d] tidings [concerning the] Man. The Man him[s]elf gave [his life to] his limbs and gathered his soul i[nto one, and] he built it in its place like this tower [that is built up whole.]

[He] shaped it and beautified it skillfully [, giving it a heavenly] for[m. And] the voices that he sent [forth, that] he might sink in and quench [the fire of darkness upon the] so[u]l that was crushed by the enemy. They were gathered in. They came, set firm once more, in the image of their father.
